questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had heard that KU Leuven was a very academic and good university to study law. Furthermore i was told by friends that had gone to Leuven before me that the study environment was very nice and that there was a opportunity to get many contacts from all over the world.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was in general easy, but the housing situation in Leuven is difficult and finding information about it even more so. We were very lucky and found something on facebook, but this was a huge stress factor.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got a lot from the exchange coordinator from KU Leuven, Daisy. Furthermore KU Leuven and their diffrent exchange organisations had arranged a lot of informationssessions were you got all the info you needed to get settled in Leuven.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard. only advice is just to keep trying.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would generally advise against living off campus. It is difficult to have good relationships and bonds with other students. We were very lucky and have had a good time socially despite living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not enough available such a stress factor

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to send our prior approval from Denmark. In addition, we had to register on their website. It was super easy with all the guides that were sent to us.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: guides and people who were there to answer questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% succesfull

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it. It's super easy and their super helpfull, if you get confused.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was a bit strange. The ECTS points don't really give a clear picture of how much work and effort you have to put into a course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I like both methods. Very nice to try a diffrent approach but like the one at UCPH as well.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Cybercrime and crime control
2) International criminal law
3) international police and judicial cooperation
4) Restorative justice
5) Juvenile justice and youth criminology
6) politicall crimes and transitional justice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: international criminal law and Juvenile justice and youth criminology

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It's easy to travel around Europe from Belgium and this is concidered a normal part of the exchange. So we used a lot of money on traveling because everyone else also does.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Partying is super cheap. Food is not that cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We played padle, Tennis and soccer

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Padle. It's cheap and super fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Tour the various cities in Belgium and travel to other major cities in Europe by train or bus. Super easy and cheap.

Flight are cheap if you go from Charleroi but would not recommend. It's expensive and hard to get to Charleroi from Leuven.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. THey're openminded and very much like Danish people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just join in on everything you get invited to and don't be afraid to talk to other people. Everybody is keen on making new friendships and shared experiences

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the locals go home every weekend to have their clothes washed and food cooked by their parents. They do not have student jobs and do not really take responsibility for their finances themselves because in most cases the parents pay. This can be hard when you have to explain that you don't hav e money yourself for everything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the social and including part.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Travel in the beginning
2) Find housing ASAP
3) Live in Leuven and preferably inside the cityring.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friendships from all over the world, learning diffrent cultures again from all over the world and finally the academics were interesting and diffrent from how you learn and what is taught at UCPH

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Exam period for sure. It's very intensense because you have so many exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
